chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Hasan al-Siql, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked and mentioned a similar [ruling], except that he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The child belongs to the one who has the girl, and he should be patient, for the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): The child belongs to the bed (of the owner), and for the adulterer is the stone.

key_terms.الْحَجَرُ: The stone (symbolizing the one who throws it, i.e., the father who claims the child)
key_terms.لِلْفِرَاشِ: To the bed (meaning the owner's bed/marital bed)

ai.seo_question: Who owns the child born to a purchased female slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabar highlights the application of 'al-waladu lil-firashi' (the child belongs to the one whose bed is shared) specifically within the context of purchasing a female slave, where the owner's right to intercourse establishes paternity. The phrase 'and he should be patient' reflects the juristic discretion of the owner to acknowledge the child or maintain the status quo, distinguishing this private ownership scenario from the general rule for free women where the child initially belongs to the mother unless paternity is formally claimed. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the 'bed' refers to the legitimate sphere of sexual access, whether through marriage or slavery, ensuring lineage clarity in pre-modern legal frameworks.
